claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To help determine your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

Are you responsible for Alex's care, and does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he doesn't actually live with me at the moment. He's been in local authority care for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's situation. Since he's in local authority care, I need to ask a couple more questions to determine your eligibility.

You mentioned Alex has been in care for a couple of months. To clarify:

Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or does he spend at least 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 days or more in a row) at your home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home to stay with me. He's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I understand this must be a difficult situation.

I have one more question: Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of this information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, I have to share some difficult news. Let me explain the outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Alex's situation:**
- Alex has been in local authority care full-time for more than 8 weeks (a couple of months).
- Under the Child Benefit rules, entitlement to Child Benefit usually ends once a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks.
- There are exceptions that would allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit, such as if Alex spent at least 24 hours a week at home, or stayed at least 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 days or more in a row) at your home. However, you've confirmed that Alex is in care full-time and doesn't come home to stay with you.

**What you can do:**
- If Alex's situation changes in the future and he begins spending regular time at home with you (such as 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row), you may become eligible again. In that case, you should contact HMRC to discuss your circumstances.

I understand this isn't the news you were hoping for, and I'm sorry. If you have any questions or if Alex's circumstances change, please don't hesitate to get in touch with the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks (a couple of months). According to the Child Benefit rules for children in care, you are usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit after the 8-week time limit. There is an exception that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, or spends at least 2 nights in a row each week (or 7 days or more in a row) at home. However, you have confirmed that Alex is in care full-time and does not come home to stay with you. Since Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks and does not meet any of the exceptions, you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
